ACCESS_CONTROL.needs: A controller, or the software beside it, that can push events out.
ACCESS_CONTROL.title: Access controller
ACCESS_CONTROL.what: Card-and-door records come in: who, when, in or out, allowed or refused. Kept unchangeable.

ACCOUNTING.needs: The accounting system's endpoint address and key, and a short piece of code on that side to read our format.
ACCOUNTING.title: Accounting software
ACCOUNTING.what: Only the money side: invoices issued, outbound shipments confirmed, weighings settled. Day-to-day vehicle movements are not sent.

AI.needs: A device that can send its conclusions in our format.
AI.title: AI analysis box
AI.what: Whatever the box concluded arrives as a reading and is kept. **We receive and store; we do not analyse** - the analysis is that device's job.

ANPR.needs: A camera that can send the plate it read, registered against one specific weighbridge.
ANPR.title: Number-plate camera
ANPR.what: The camera reads a plate and sends it in; we check it against the orders waiting. A match is let through, and the LED board, the voice unit and the barrier are told. No match is not let through, and the operator is asked.

API_GATEWAY.title: Your own gateway
API_GATEWAY.what: If your company runs a middle layer, everything can go through it: it can push your devices' data in, and it can receive what we send out. Both directions.

CCTV.needs: The camera or recorder must be able to push images out. **An RTSP stream on its own is not enough** - that is a picture, and it never tells us that something happened.
CCTV.title: Camera or recorder
CCTV.what: The camera sends stills and clips in, kept as evidence alongside the paperwork.

DRONE.needs: A ground station or software that can push the record out.
DRONE.title: Drone
DRONE.what: After a flight, the log and any readings are sent in and kept. **We do not fly it, plan a route, or handle take-off and landing** - only the record.

ERP.needs: An endpoint address and a key from your ERP supplier. What we send is our own format, so someone on that side writes a short piece of code to read it.
ERP.title: Your company's own ERP system
ERP.what: Sends a copy of what happens here into the ERP your office already uses - a load weighed, an order accepted, an invoice issued - so nobody has to type it in a second time.

FACE_RECOGNITION.needs: A unit that can output its own person reference, matched to the people on this platform.
FACE_RECOGNITION.title: Face recognition unit
FACE_RECOGNITION.what: Once the unit recognises somebody, it sends us who it was. **Only the person's reference, never the face image** - the picture stays on your equipment.

GOVERNMENT_API.needs: The authority's endpoint address and key. As above, we send our general format; the specific form needs translating.
GOVERNMENT_API.title: Government or authority endpoint
GOVERNMENT_API.what: Reports where the waste went: the lorry loaded and left, the weighbridge settled, the shipment confirmed. Those three are exactly the trail an authority follows.

IOT.needs: A sensor or its gateway that can send in our format and sign what it sends.
IOT.title: Sensors
IOT.what: Readings such as temperature, fuel level or vibration, sent in on a schedule and kept.

MYINVOIS.needs: Credentials from the tax authority. Note: what leaves here is our general format, **not yet the form the authority specifies** - a translation step in between has to be provided by you or your supplier.
MYINVOIS.title: Malaysian e-invoicing (MyInvois)
MYINVOIS.what: Sends an invoice onward the moment it is issued.

RF.needs: A monitor that can push its observations out.
RF.title: Radio anti-tamper monitor
RF.what: Suspicious radio signals near the weighbridge come in and sit beside that load's weighing record, which is how remote-control tampering shows up.

RFID.needs: A reader or its controller that can push the reads out.
RFID.title: RFID cards
RFID.what: Worker and vehicle cards, read and sent in, kept with the rest of the gate record.

TOWER_CRANE.needs: A crane monitor that can push readings out.
TOWER_CRANE.title: Tower crane monitor
TOWER_CRANE.what: Load, wind speed and radius readings are sent in and kept, so there is a record if anything happens. **No moment interlock, no part in any safety control** - that belongs to the crane's own system and must never depend on an instruction from the internet.

VISITOR_MANAGEMENT.needs: A visitor system that can push its events out.
VISITOR_MANAGEMENT.title: Visitor system
VISITOR_MANAGEMENT.what: Visitor sign-in and movements come in, kept in the same place as the workers' record.

WEBHOOK.needs: An address that can receive a web request. Leave it in simulated mode first and you can see what would be sent without connecting anything real.
WEBHOOK.title: General notifications (webhook)
WEBHOOK.what: The simplest one. When something happens here, we post a notification to an address you choose and you do what you like with it. Best for a company with no ERP, and the easiest way to see what we would send.

activity_logs.what: What people did in the system, newest first, searchable.
activity_logs.trouble: Cannot find an action: if it truly is not here, it went through a read path that leaves no row.

approvals.what: The approval chains themselves, and the record of every decision taken through them.
approvals.who: Holders of approval.view; deciding needs approval.review.
approvals.need: A chain needs a name, and each level needs a level name and an approver. A manual approval record needs a title, the record type, the record id and a note.
approvals.then: Each level is notified in turn as the one before it decides.
approvals.trouble: A chain with no approver on a level will stall there. Every level needs a person.

asset_management.what: The platform's own kit: what was bought, who holds it, where it is installed, what has been repaired and what has been written off.
asset_management.need: An asset needs a category, a name, a serial number, purchase details and a price. A loan needs the asset, the holder, the date and the purpose; a return needs the actual date and the condition. A transfer needs the destination, the date and a reason. A write-off needs a reason, a disposal method and someone's approve-or-reject note.
asset_management.then: Every movement joins the asset's history, so its page reads as one line from purchase to write-off.
asset_management.trouble: Transfer and loan are easy to mix up: a transfer moves the asset to another place while it stays the company's; a loan puts it in a person's hands and it has to come back.

attendance.what: Who clocked in where, with the selfie and the location taken at the time.
attendance.need: Clocking in from the phone needs today's project, a selfie and the current GPS fix. All three.
attendance.then: The clock-in is judged against the site's geofence and stored with both.
attendance.trouble: GPS refusing to fix: step outside or to the gate and try again. The system will not use an inaccurate position to make the number up.

audit_log_center.what: Who did what, when. Three layers: sign-ins, the audit trail, and the permanent record that cannot be deleted at all.
audit_log_center.then: Nothing. These pages are read-only, including for platform administrators. That is the point of them.
audit_log_center.trouble: Cannot find an action: the trail is newest-first and searchable. If it truly is not there, that action went through a read path that leaves no audit row.

billing_commission.what: The platform's two kinds of money, kept apart: the SaaS subscription a company pays, and the commission the platform takes from recycling trades.
billing_commission.who: Holders of billing.view; confirming a receipt needs billing.collect.
billing_commission.need: Recording a payment by hand needs the invoice number, the amount and the date paid. Reviewing one needs a review note.
billing_commission.then: A recorded payment sits as pending until a person confirms or rejects it. Receiving a proof never marks an invoice paid on its own.
billing_commission.trouble: Commission that looks wrong is usually read against the wrong side: it follows the recycler's plan, not the contractor's.

cloud_service_management.what: The cloud the platform buys: which vendor, what was bought, how much was used this month, what it cost, and whether the budget is blown. Alibaba Cloud, Azure and Linode can pull their usage back automatically.
cloud_service_management.need: A service needs a vendor, a type, a name, a description and a contract start date. Recording usage by hand needs the service, the date, the amount and its unit. A budget needs a year, a month and the monthly figure.
cloud_service_management.then: Usage sync runs in the background; each run records whether it worked and how many rows it pulled.
cloud_service_management.trouble: Usage stuck at zero: that vendor's credentials, tenant id included, are incomplete. The sync record says exactly why it failed. Fill them in and trigger a run.

cloud_weighing.what: Every weighbridge on the network from the platform's side: where it is, whether it is talking, whether a lorry is on it now, and any strange readings.
cloud_weighing.then: Opening one weighing shows the whole weight curve, not just the final figure. A settlement number you cannot check for yourself is only an invoice.
cloud_weighing.trouble: A bridge showing offline: check the last-contact time on the connections page. The wiring and parameter crib for the site end is on that weighbridge's gateway panel.

company_management.what: Open new companies, review their papers, and see each one's projects and recycler partners. Nothing else in the platform exists until a company does.
company_management.who: Platform roles holding company.view. Opening a new one also needs company.create.
company_management.need: The bank step will not pass without bank name, account name and account number; the licence step needs a PDF or image.
company_management.then: The company's starting roles are created automatically and an activation email goes to its first administrator.
company_management.trouble: If they say no email arrived, the server's mail host is not configured. Copy the activation link from the company page and send it yourself.

company_settings.what: Your own company's details, its sites, and the links you hand to people outside the company.
company_settings.need: A site needs a code, a name and an address. An external link needs a name, what it shows and an expiry. Bank details need the bank name, the account holder and the account number.
company_settings.then: An external link works for anyone holding it until its expiry, then stops on its own.
company_settings.trouble: An external link that has stopped working has expired. Make a new one - they never renew themselves, which is deliberate.

consultant_applications.what: The consultant side: raising applications, walking them through an approval chain, signing them, and the field evidence that supports them.
consultant_applications.who: Holders of approval.view. Configuring flows needs consultant.config, raising one needs consultant.submit, deciding needs approval.review.
consultant_applications.need: An application needs the project, the workflow, the type, the discipline, the inspection type, the priority, the consultant and their firm, the location, the element or work area, the description and the form template. A decision needs your six-digit approval PIN and a note. Setting that PIN needs your current password, the new PIN twice and a signature.
consultant_applications.then: A PIN plus a signature is a signature. It cannot be undone.
consultant_applications.trouble: Approval buttons greyed out means you have not set your approval PIN yet. Consultants seeing no projects have authorisation that has expired or was never given for that project - it is granted per project with a start and an end.

customer_management.what: Where your material comes from: contractors you have a platform partnership with, and private customers who simply drive in.
customer_management.need: A customer needs a company name. Regenerating their QR code needs a reason. A private intake needs the customer's QR code, the yard and the material, and closing it needs the weighing to be done.
customer_management.then: Each customer has a QR code; scanning it at the gate attaches the incoming lorry to them.
customer_management.trouble: Platform commission follows your own plan - partner or standard - not the contractor's. That is the usual source of a figure that looks wrong.

customer_service.what: The customer relationship side: enquiries, training, visits, feedback and service records, all hanging off the customer's file.
customer_service.need: A customer needs a company name, a contact and an email. An enquiry needs a subject and a body. A visit needs the date, who you met, the purpose and the goal. Marking a customer lost needs the reason.
customer_service.then: Everything lands on that customer's file, so their page shows the whole history in order.
customer_service.trouble: Cannot find a customer: customers here are the platform's customers, meaning the companies. A recycler's own walk-in customers live in that recycler's back office.

dashboard.what: Today at a glance: what is waiting for you, what is running, and how the system itself is doing.
dashboard.who: Anyone who can sign in. No extra permission needed.
dashboard.then: Each card opens the module behind it. Nothing is edited here.
dashboard.trouble: A number here disagreeing with a report is almost always a different date range. The report page lets you choose one; trust that.

documents.what: Filed documents, in one place, with their categories.
documents.need: A document needs a title, a category and the file itself. A category needs a code and a name.
documents.then: It is filed and searchable by title and category.
documents.trouble: Nothing common enough to warn about yet.

driver_gps.what: Where your lorries are right now, and the track each one has taken.
driver_gps.then: The track is drawn from what the phone actually reported.
driver_gps.trouble: A gap in a track is normal - phone browsers stop reporting when the screen locks. The gap is left as a gap on purpose: joining the two ends would draw a road nobody recorded.

driver_tasks.what: Every trip assigned to your drivers and where each one has got to.
driver_tasks.then: Each step the driver presses on the phone shows here and on the contractor's side at the same time.
driver_tasks.trouble: A trip that has not moved for a while: check driver GPS before calling. He may be waiting at a gate.

drivers.what: Your drivers and the lorry each one normally takes.
drivers.who: Holders of yard.view; changing the fleet needs fleet.manage.
drivers.need: A driver needs a default vehicle. A driver with no lorry is half a record, so the form will not save without one.
drivers.then: Once created they get the driver app and can be assigned trips.
drivers.trouble: The driver form will not save: you have not picked a default vehicle.

emergency_list.what: Who is still inside the site right now, with a number you can call. For a headcount when something has gone wrong.
emergency_list.then: The list refreshes on its own. Tapping a number dials it.
emergency_list.trouble: Someone missing from the list has already been scanned out, or never scanned in. The gate events say which.

equipment.what: The plant on site: which site it is at and what condition it is in.
equipment.need: A code, a name and the project it belongs to.
equipment.then: It joins that site's equipment list and its reports.
equipment.trouble: Nothing common enough to warn about yet.

evidence.what: The photos, signatures and locations that back up every record - kept where they cannot be quietly changed.
evidence.need: Replacing a piece of evidence needs a written reason and the replacement file.
evidence.then: Nothing here can be edited or deleted. A replacement leaves the original in place, marked as replaced, so the correction is visible rather than invisible.
evidence.trouble: Uploaded the wrong thing and want it gone: it cannot go. That is the design. Replace it and say why.

field_tasks.what: Jobs sent to a named person on site: where, what, and how many photos it takes to close.
field_tasks.who: Holders of project.view; assigning needs task.assign.
field_tasks.need: A task needs the project, a title and the site person it goes to.
field_tasks.then: It appears on that person's phone immediately, with the photo count it needs.
field_tasks.trouble: Submitted work coming back rejected repeatedly usually means the instruction was too vague. The site sees only what you typed.

geofences.what: The boundary drawn around a site, which decides whether a clock-in counts as on site.
geofences.need: A fence needs the project, a name and at least three boundary points. The button says how many more you still need.
geofences.then: From then on, attendance is judged against it.
geofences.trouble: A fence drawn too tight rejects honest clock-ins at the gate. Leave a margin.

hazard_rectification.what: Hazards found on site, who has to fix them, and the photo that proves it was fixed.
hazard_rectification.who: Holders of both safety.view and project.view.
hazard_rectification.need: Assigning needs the person responsible, a deadline and the location. Reporting it done needs what was completed. Signing it off needs an acceptance photo and a note.
hazard_rectification.then: No acceptance photo, no closure. A hazard is not fixed because someone said so.
hazard_rectification.trouble: Nothing common enough to warn about yet.

integrations.what: Connections to your own systems and hardware: ERP, accounting, gates, cameras, and the commands sent to devices.
integrations.need: A connection needs a name and a base URL. Sending a device command needs the device number and the command body.
integrations.then: A command sits as waiting until the device answers. Only acknowledged means the controller actually did it.
integrations.trouble: No answer means the device never replied - not that it refused. Refused is a different status, and so is closed by hand.

inventory_management.what: How much of each material is in the yard right now.
inventory_management.need: Adjusting a figure by hand needs the adjustment in kilograms and a written reason.
inventory_management.then: Intake adds to the figure and confirmed outbound takes from it, so the number moves on its own most of the time.
inventory_management.trouble: Stock not matching the yard: look for manual adjustments first. Every one carries a reason, so you can see who changed what and why.

material_cost_report.what: What the materials cost, per category and per project.
material_cost_report.then: The totals are money, accumulated from the delivery orders behind each receipt.
material_cost_report.trouble: A total that looks low: check the missing-prices column. Materials received without a unit price are not counted, so the sum understates until you fill them in.

material_outgoing.what: Material leaving site again - returns to the supplier, or moves elsewhere.
material_outgoing.need: The project, the supplier, the material, the quantity, the reason for sending it back (with the detail if you choose Other), the evidence photos, the receiver's signature, the supplier's signature and where it goes.
material_outgoing.then: Both signatures are captured on the phone and stored with the record. It cannot be edited afterwards.
material_outgoing.trouble: The signature pad ignores a fine stylus. Use a finger.

material_quantity_report.what: How much of each material came in and went out, over a period you choose.
material_quantity_report.then: Exporting leaves a row in the export history.
material_quantity_report.trouble: An empty report usually means nothing was received in that range.

material_receipts.what: Material arriving on site, and the material categories - the budget and the spend for each material. The budget here is money accumulated from delivery orders, not a tonnage.
material_receipts.need: Receiving on site needs the project, the code, the name, a photo of the delivery order, the person handling it, the quantity, a site photo and the current GPS fix.
material_receipts.then: A submitted receipt cannot be edited - it carries photos, a signature and a location. To correct one, void it and raise a new one.
material_receipts.trouble: Delivery order says one quantity and the lorry brought another: enter what actually arrived. Both figures are kept, so the difference is on the record rather than hidden.

notification_center.what: What the platform sends to companies: the message, the channel it went out on, and whether it arrived.
notification_center.need: Sending one needs the receiving companies, a title, the body and a category.
notification_center.then: Sent is sent. There is no recall, so check who is on the list before you press it.
notification_center.trouble: Nobody received it: open the notification records and read that row's channel status. Email failing is almost always an unconfigured mail host.

notifications.what: What has been sent to you, and what you send to your own people.
notifications.need: Sending one needs the project, the recipients, a title and the body.
notifications.then: Sent is sent - there is no recall.
notifications.trouble: Nothing common enough to warn about yet.

outbound_management.what: Buyers and shipments: who you sell to and what has gone out.
outbound_management.who: Holders of inventory.view; shipping needs outbound.manage.
outbound_management.need: A shipment needs the buyer, the weight and the date. Confirming it needs the e-invoice number. A buyer needs a company name.
outbound_management.then: Confirming takes the weight off stock immediately and creates the matching e-invoice record.
outbound_management.trouble: A shipment stuck in draft has not been confirmed, so it has not touched stock yet.

partner_management.what: The platform's channel partners: agents and resellers, their territories, agreements, commission schemes and performance.
partner_management.need: A partner needs a name, a contact, a phone, an email and a start date. An agreement needs a title, a description, its terms, an effective date and the document. Changing status needs a reason.
partner_management.then: An uploaded agreement is archived; replacing one keeps the earlier version.
partner_management.trouble: Partner customer assignment and sales customer assignment are different things - one is customers a channel brought in, the other is customers an internal salesperson owns. The same company can appear in both.

partnerships.what: The contractors you have agreed to take material from, and on what terms.
partnerships.need: Both sides of the pairing have to be chosen before it can be saved.
partnerships.then: Once agreed, that contractor can send you orders.
partnerships.trouble: No orders arriving from a contractor you expected: check the partnership is active, not just created.

payment_proofs.what: Proof that the recycler has paid for a load, and where each one stands.
payment_proofs.need: Marking one paid needs the paid amount.
payment_proofs.then: A confirmed proof closes that load's settlement.
payment_proofs.trouble: Amounts that do not match are usually a deduction you have not read yet - open the load and look at whether anything was deducted.

payment_status.what: What is owed on each load and what has been paid.
payment_status.need: Marking a settlement paid needs the amount paid.
payment_status.then: The load closes once the payment is confirmed on both sides.
payment_status.trouble: A settlement that looks short: open the load and check whether a deduction was raised against it.

platform_monitoring.what: The platform's own health: live load, weighbridge links, outside integrations, data sync, exceptions and scheduled jobs.
platform_monitoring.who: Platform staff holding platform.monitor. This is an internal support area and is deliberately kept out of the customer sidebar.
platform_monitoring.need: Closing an exception needs a handling note. A new scheduled job needs a code, a name, an owner, a first run time and an interval in minutes.
platform_monitoring.then: Run now really runs it. This is not a rehearsal.
platform_monitoring.trouble: An empty CCTV, ANPR or gateway page is not broken - that customer simply has none of that hardware connected. These are integrations you buy, not things every site has.

platform_settings.what: The platform's master switches: base parameters, the default SaaS and commission rules, weighbridge parameters, hardware integrations, releases, maintenance notices and feature switches.
platform_settings.need: A release needs a module, a version, change notes and an English release note. A maintenance notice needs a title and a body. A feature switch needs a key.
platform_settings.then: A feature switch takes effect across the whole platform at once - for everyone, for a percentage, or for named companies. Think about the blast radius first.
platform_settings.trouble: Changed the commission settings and old invoices did not move: correct. You changed the rule going forward. Issued invoices are records and are never rewritten.

progress.what: How far the work actually is, reported from site with a photo and a location.
progress.who: Holders of both progress.view and project.view.
progress.need: A report needs the project, a title and the percentage complete. From the phone it also needs the stage, a site photo and the current GPS fix.
progress.then: The figure lands against that stage and feeds the progress report.
progress.trouble: No signal on site is fine - shoot and fill anyway, it queues and uploads later. The location stored is where you were when you took the photo, not where you were when it finally sent.

project_categories.what: The categories under each business entry: concrete and rebar under material categories, safety-department rectification under hazard categories.
project_categories.need: A category needs its business entry, the project, a code, a name, and who may see it.
project_categories.then: Site staff can choose it when they submit on the phone, and the office can file records into it.
project_categories.trouble: A category cannot be picked on the phone: check that it is active and not restricted to other people.

projects.what: Project files, the tasks sent out to site, and the photos coming back for approval. Everything else in this back office hangs off a project.
projects.who: Holders of project.view; creating one needs project.create.
projects.need: A project needs its code, name and address. Adding someone to the team needs the person and their role on it.
projects.then: Only after a project exists can site staff pick it on their phone.
projects.trouble: Site staff cannot see a project on their phone: nine times out of ten they were never added to its team. When you send a photo back, the reason you type appears on their task card, so write something they can act on.

qr_code_management.what: The codes the platform issues - on vehicles, people and stockpiles - who scanned them, when, and which scans went wrong.
qr_code_management.need: Issuing a code needs the thing it is bound to and an expiry date. Voiding one needs a reason.
qr_code_management.then: A voided code stops scanning immediately; its past scans stay on record.
qr_code_management.trouble: Scanned and nothing happened: look at the anomalies page. Nearly always the code has expired, or the person scanning lacks the permission.

recyclers.what: The whole waste chain from this side: which recyclers you work with, applying to send waste out, the resulting orders, site clearance and payment proofs.
recyclers.need: Pairing with a recycler needs you to pick the recycler and the project.
recyclers.then: Once paired, that recycler can be chosen when you send waste out.
recyclers.trouble: A recycler missing from the dropdown has not been paired with that project yet.

recycling_records.what: The weighing of your own loads: the full weight curve for each lorry that left your site, not just the final number.
recycling_records.who: Holders of weighing.view - site supervisors and project managers have it by default.
recycling_records.then: Opening one shows the curve, so you can satisfy yourself the lorry stood still long enough for the reading to be real.
recycling_records.trouble: You see only weighings attached to your own loads. The yard's own calibration and tare runs stay private to the yard, which is right - they are nobody else's business.

report_center.what: Platform-level reports, and the history of everything anyone has exported.
report_center.need: Choose a date range before exporting.
report_center.then: An export writes a file and a history row: who exported what, when.
report_center.trouble: An empty export usually means there really is nothing in that range, or two filters that cannot both be true at once.

roles.what: What each role in your company is allowed to see and do.
roles.who: Holders of role.view; editing needs role.update.
roles.need: A role needs a code, a name and at least one permission.
roles.then: Permission changes take effect the next time that person loads a page. They may need to refresh.
roles.trouble: Someone sees an empty sidebar: their role has no module permissions at all.

safety.what: Safety events on site: logging them and reporting them up.
safety.who: Holders of both safety.view and project.view.
safety.need: An event needs the project, the safety category, a title, photos, GPS evidence, the people responsible and what was done. A report needs the project, a title, what happened, who it goes to, the evidence and the place.
safety.then: The people named are notified straight away.
safety.trouble: Photos and GPS are both required and there is often no signal. Shoot anyway - it queues and uploads later, and the location kept is where you stood when you took it.

sales_commission.what: The platform's own sales team: who covers which territory, whose customers they are, what they earn and when it is settled.
sales_commission.need: A commission rule needs a name, a calculation basis and an effective date. Recording a payout needs a payment reference.
sales_commission.then: A confirmed settlement locks. After that the only correction is an offsetting entry, never an edit.
sales_commission.trouble: Territories are one list, not two. The entry here opens the partner territories page, so both sides always show the same rows.

schedule.what: The WBS programme, which can be brought in from Excel and revised over time.
schedule.who: Holders of both progress.view and project.view.
schedule.need: An import needs an .xlsx file, a plan name and a revision name; revising a confirmed plan also needs the reason for the change. A task added by hand needs its WBS, name, planned start and planned finish.
schedule.then: Importing is two steps. The preview reads your headers and lets you map the columns, and writes nothing - you can try it safely. Only Confirm import writes.
schedule.trouble: An import that will not go through is usually missing a mapping: WBS, task name and planned start are required, plus either planned finish or a duration.

site_access.what: Site passes - who may come in and when - and the gate desk that scans them.
site_access.who: Holders of site_access.view; issuing and revoking need site_access.manage.
site_access.need: A pass needs the project, the purpose of entry, valid-from and valid-until times and a name; a vehicle pass also needs the plate. The gate desk needs a scanner or a pasted credential - a card number, a plate or a system number.
site_access.then: A pass takes effect only after approval, and a revoked one stops scanning immediately.
site_access.trouble: A scan that comes back denied says why in the device events - expired, not approved, or not for this site.

site_disposals.what: Clearing rubbish and debris off site - the job that is not a recyclable load.
site_disposals.need: The request needs the project, a description of the rubbish, the site location, a site photo and the current GPS fix. Completing it needs the actual weight in kilograms, the disposal DO number and the trip count.
site_disposals.then: Approving it produces a task link with an expiry, which the crew opens to do the job.
site_disposals.trouble: The task link stops working after its expiry. Cancelling one needs a reason on the record.

site_gps.what: Where your people are on site right now.
site_gps.then: The map shows the last position each person reported.
site_gps.trouble: Nobody on the map: phone browsers stop reporting when the screen locks, so gaps are normal. A gap is drawn as a gap - the system will not join two points into a road nobody travelled.

subscription_management.what: The SaaS plans themselves - price, what is included, what the limits are - and which company is on which plan until when.
subscription_management.need: A plan needs a code, a name, an audience (contractor or recycler), a billing cycle and its fee.
subscription_management.then: Changing a price does not touch invoices already issued. Those are financial records, so they are never rewritten behind your back.
subscription_management.trouble: Plan changed but the customer still cannot use the new feature: subscriptions take effect per company. Check the company subscriptions page, not just the plan definition.

suppliers.what: Supplier files, and each supplier's short code at each site.
suppliers.need: A supplier needs a name and contact details. Setting a site code needs you to pick the site first.
suppliers.then: Site codes show up in the receiving screen's dropdown, which is faster to pick from than full names.
suppliers.trouble: A supplier missing from the site's dropdown was never attached to that site.

technical_support.what: Tickets: problems customers report, bugs, API work, weighbridge installations and equipment maintenance.
technical_support.need: Every ticket needs a title and a body. An installation ticket also needs a place and a date.
technical_support.then: A status change notifies whoever raised it.
technical_support.trouble: Nothing common enough to warn about yet.

transaction_reports.what: Intake, outbound, deductions and settlements, over a period you choose.
transaction_reports.then: Exporting leaves a row in the export history.
transaction_reports.trouble: An empty export usually means nothing happened in that range.

user_logs.what: Sign-in history: who signed in, from where, and when.
user_logs.trouble: Nothing common enough to warn about yet.

user_management.what: Platform-side accounts: who may sign in to Admin, and as what. Each company's own staff are managed by that company, not here.
user_management.who: Holders of user.view; adding and editing need user.create and user.update.
user_management.then: They get an activation email and set their own password. You can never see or set someone else's password, only resend the invitation.
user_management.trouble: Someone signs in and sees nothing: their role carries no module permissions. Tick some on the roles page.

users.what: Your company's own staff accounts, their roles, sign-in history and handovers.
users.who: Holders of user.view; changing roles needs role.update.
users.need: A user needs a name and an email. A handover needs the reason for it.
users.then: A handover moves the open work to whoever takes over, and leaves a record of it.
users.trouble: The company administrator role cannot be deleted. That is deliberate - otherwise it is possible to delete the only role that can manage users and lock everyone out.

vehicles.what: Your lorries, and the tare weight of each one.
vehicles.who: Holders of yard.view; changing the fleet needs fleet.manage.
vehicles.need: A vehicle needs its plate and its tare weight in kilograms. Changing a tare weight needs a written reason.
vehicles.then: Tare feeds straight into every net weight that lorry produces, which is why changing it leaves a record.
vehicles.trouble: Net weights all shifting by the same amount usually means someone changed a tare. The reason is on the record.

waste_dispatches.what: The orders themselves, once a recycler has been assigned: where each load is now, and who has it.
waste_dispatches.need: Releasing a load needs the photo and the name of the person releasing it.
waste_dispatches.then: The order moves through collected, weighed and settled, and each step is visible to both sides.
waste_dispatches.trouble: An order that seems stuck is usually waiting on the recycler to assign a lorry. The order page shows whose move it is.

waste_orders.what: Orders arriving from contractors: assigning a lorry and a driver, and following each load.
waste_orders.who: Holders of dispatch.view; assigning needs dispatch.update.
waste_orders.need: Assigning needs a vehicle and a driver.
waste_orders.then: The trip appears on that driver's phone straight away, with the pickup address and a navigate button.
waste_orders.trouble: Driver says the navigation is wrong: the address came from the contractor's application, or from the project when they left it blank. The order page shows which of the two it is.

waste_outgoing.what: Asking to send a load of waste off site. This is the head of the chain: it becomes the order the recycler receives.
waste_outgoing.need: The project, the waste category, the quantity and photos of the waste. Assigning it needs the recycler; handing it on needs who to and a note; rejecting needs a reason; confirming the final collection needs the date and time.
waste_outgoing.then: The pickup address travels with the order. Leave it blank and the project's address is used; type one and the driver's navigation goes where you typed. Someone editing the project address later never rewrites an order already sent - where a collected load came from is a fixed fact.
waste_outgoing.trouble: Driver navigating to the wrong place: whatever is on the application is where he goes. The list marks which addresses were typed by a person.

weighbridges.what: The bridges themselves: where each is, what it talks, and whether it is connected.
weighbridges.who: Holders of weighing.view; changing one needs scale.manage.
weighbridges.need: A bridge needs a code, a name, its yard and its protocol.
weighbridges.then: Once connected it starts feeding readings into the weighing desk.
weighbridges.trouble: Offline: the gateway panel on the bridge page carries the wiring and the settings to check, in the order to check them.

weighing_records.what: The weighbridge desk: every weighing with its full curve, the bridges themselves, deductions, and where each settlement stands.
weighing_records.who: Holders of weighing.view; operating the bridge needs weighing.operate; raising a deduction needs deduction.create.
weighing_records.need: Releasing at the desk needs the bridge and the outgoing order number; confirming needs the release time. A deduction needs its photo, and the contractor's answer to it needs their response.
weighing_records.then: Confirming a ticket moves that order to weighed. A deduction is optional: with nothing to deduct, settlement runs on the full net weight. You can still raise one after weighing - the scissors button on each row opens the form with that load already chosen.
weighing_records.trouble: A weighbridge showing offline: check the gateway panel on that bridge, which carries the DTU wiring and parameter crib for whoever is standing at it.

yards.what: Your yards - the places material comes into and goes out of.
yards.who: Holders of yard.view; changing them needs yard.manage.
yards.need: A yard needs a code, a name and an address.
yards.then: A yard becomes selectable on intake, weighing and inventory screens.
yards.trouble: Nothing common enough to warn about yet.
